answer: The basalt multiplier is published, charged in canyon, and summit lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 9 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3321 identities would post 1328 proofs and burn roughly 32 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
